faqs.a: Sources disagree, some care guides recommend a moderate 40 to 60% for many commonly kept dry-adapted species, while others suggest 65 to 75%. In practice, a reliable water dish combined with lightly moistened substrate is more consistent than heavy misting, which raises mold risk without a clear benefit.

faqs.q: Can you house multiple tarantulas together?
faqs.a: No. Most species are solitary and cannibalistic, so cohabitation isn't a workable setup regardless of enclosure size, house tarantulas singly.

title: Tarantula vs. Emperor Scorpion: Which Invertebrate Actually Fits You
seoTitle: Tarantula vs. Emperor Scorpion: Full Comparison
excerpt: Tarantula or emperor scorpion? The differences in defense mechanisms, whether they lay eggs or give live birth, and just how differently males and females age, not just which one looks scarier.
imageAlt: A tarantula and an emperor scorpion side by side for comparison
author: Michael Ryan

faqs.q: Is a tarantula or an emperor scorpion more dangerous to keep?
faqs.a: Neither is dangerous for the commonly kept beginner species. The New World tarantulas most often sold as pets have venom about as mild as a wasp sting and defend mainly with barbed urticating hairs, not a bite. Emperor scorpions do have a true venomous sting, but scientists consider it mild, comparable to a bee sting, since the species relies on its large pincers rather than its stinger for both defense and hunting.

faqs.q: Do tarantulas and emperor scorpions reproduce the same way?
faqs.a: No, this is one of the clearest biological differences between them. Female tarantulas lay eggs, sometimes hundreds at once, inside a silk egg sac. Emperor scorpions give live birth instead, after roughly nine months of gestation, and the 10 to 12 newborns climb onto their mother's back and stay there until they're old enough to be on their own.

faqs.q: Why do female tarantulas live so much longer than males?
faqs.a: It comes down to molting. Female tarantulas keep molting throughout their entire adult life, which is part of what lets them keep growing and living for decades. Males stop molting once they mature, and most die within about a year of reaching maturity and mating. A female of a popular pet species can live 15 to 30 years; a male of the same species often lives only 3 to 6.

faqs.q: Do emperor scorpions glow?
faqs.a: Yes. Emperor scorpions, like most scorpion species, fluoresce a pastel blue-green color under ultraviolet light, a well-documented trait used by researchers to survey wild scorpion populations at night. It has nothing to do with mood or health, every healthy emperor scorpion does it under a blacklight.

faqs.q: Which is easier to handle, a tarantula or an emperor scorpion?
faqs.a: Neither is recommended for regular handling, for different reasons. A dropped tarantula, even from a short height, can rupture its abdomen and die, making a fall far more dangerous to the animal than any bite risk to the keeper. An emperor scorpion's pincers and mild sting make it a real, if minor, pinch and sting risk to a keeper, so most keepers view both as look-don't-handle pets.

title: Tardigrades: The Toughest Creatures on Earth (And in Space)
seoTitle: Tardigrades: The Nearly Indestructible Water Bears
excerpt: Meet the tardigrade: a microscopic, eight-legged animal that has survived space, radiation, and very likely every mass extinction in Earth's history. Nature's ultimate survivor.
imageAlt: A tardigrade (water bear) viewed under a scanning electron microscope, showing its distinctive stubby legs and barrel-shaped body
author: Michael Ryan
myth: A tardigrade can survive anything, indefinitely.
truth: Dried ones collapse past about 120 days. Every multi-decade survival on record was frozen, and the two states get confused constantly.

title: The Incredible Axolotl - Nature’s Smiling Salamander
seoTitle: Axolotl Care Guide: Nature's Smiling Salamander
excerpt: Meet the axolotl, the smiling 'walking fish' that regenerates its own limbs and stays a baby forever. Why scientists adore this salamander.
imageAlt: A cute pink axolotl with feathery gills swimming in clear water
author: Michael Ryan
myth: The axolotl never grows up.
truth: It reaches full adult size and breeds. The word is paedomorphosis, and the right hormone pushes it through metamorphosis anyway.

title: The Octopus Has Three Hearts (And Uses All of Them)
seoTitle: The Octopus With Three Hearts & Blue Blood
excerpt: Did you know octopuses have three hearts and blue blood? These creatures are here to remind us nature is far stranger and more wonderful than we ever imagined.
imageAlt: A vibrant octopus gliding through colorful coral reef waters, its iridescent purple and teal arms spread wide in the deep blue ocean
author: Michael Ryan
myth: An octopus has nine brains, one in each arm.
truth: It has one, a ring around its throat, plus a nerve cord running down every arm. That is remarkable enough without the upgrade.

seoTitle: Platypus Facts: Nature's Bizarre Mammal
excerpt: Egg-laying, venomous, and able to sense electricity; the platypus breaks every mammal rule. Meet nature's most wonderfully weird animal.
